subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` contract now, and should Lossless/LCM `summaryModel` fallbacks be core-owned or plugin-owned?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the request adds a public config surface and crosses embedded compaction, model/auth routing, and context-engine plugin ownership, which repository policy treats as maintainer product direction rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve Split Ownership
options.body: Add an embedded-core compaction fallback list with explicit semantics, and require Lossless/LCM to expose any `summaryModel` fallback behavior through its plugin/context-engine contract.

options.title: Design One Summary Fallback Contract
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one shared fallback API for embedded compaction, context-engine compaction, and plugin summaries.

options.title: Keep Exact Summary Models
options.body: Decline new core config for now and leave fallback behavior to operator-managed providers, proxies, or plugin-specific implementations.

recommendation.title: Approve Split Ownership
recommendation.body: Add an embedded-core compaction fallback list with explicit semantics, and require Lossless/LCM to expose any `summaryModel` fallback behavior through its plugin/context-engine contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model-fallback, Codex compaction, and current compaction routing history make him the best available owner for the provider-routing side of the decision.
